prompt: A rancher has $120$ meters of fence to build a rectangular pen against a long barn. The barn forms one side, so only three sides need fence. What is the maximum possible area of the pen, in square meters?
hint: Let $x$ be the length of each side perpendicular to the barn. Two of those plus one parallel side use all $120$ m.

hints.text: Let $x$ be the length of each side perpendicular to the barn. Two of those plus one parallel side use all $120$ m.
$120 - 4x = 0$ gives $x = 30$. The pen is $30 \times 60$, area $1800$ m$^2$.

explanation: Area: $A(x) = x(120 - 2x) = 120x - 2x^2$. Then $A'(x) = 120 - 4x = 0$ at $x = 30$; $A'' = -4 < 0$ confirms a maximum.
$y = 120 - 60 = 60$. Maximum area $= 30 \cdot 60 = 1800$ m$^2$. The free barn side lets the pen be twice as long as it is deep.

alternativeExplanations.title: Split the fence in half
steps: At the optimum, the two perpendicular sides together use $60$ m and the parallel side uses $60$ m — the fence splits evenly between the two directions.
That is a general pattern in these problems: the fence budget divides equally between "across" and "along."
